L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n},\; L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m},

with the generators satisfying unitary commutation rules
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}=\sum_{k,l} u_{i,j,k,l}\, L_{f_l}L_{e_k},

Nonselfadjoint operator algebras of this type are constructed from two families of generators,
\[
L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n}
\quad \text{and} \quad
L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}.
\]
These generators may be thought of as representing two different kinds of directed edges, often denoted by \(e\)-edges and \(f\)-edges. The algebra generated by them is nonselfadjoint because, in general, it is generated only by these operators and not necessarily by their adjoints.

The interaction between the two families of generators is governed by a system of unitary commutation relations. These relations are determined by an \(nm \times nm\) unitary matrix
\[
u = \big(u_{i,j,k,l}\big),
\]
where the indices \(i,k\) range from \(1\) to \(n\), and the indices \(j,l\) range from \(1\) to \(m\). The matrix \(u\) encodes how products involving an \(e\)-generator followed by an \(f\)-generator can be rewritten as linear combinations of products in the opposite order.

The defining relation is
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{n}\sum_{l=1}^{m}
u_{i,j,k,l}\, L_{f_l}L_{e_k},
\]
for all \(1 \leq i \leq n\) and \(1 \leq j \leq m\). Thus, instead of requiring the generators to commute in the usual sense, the algebra allows a twisted or unitary form of commutation. The unitary matrix \(u\) ensures that this change of order is compatible with the Hilbert space structure and gives a well-behaved operator algebra.

These algebras generalise the analytic Toeplitz algebras associated with rank 2 graphs having a single vertex. In the rank 2 graph setting, the commutation relations are typically determined by a permutation rule describing how an \(e\)-edge followed by an \(f\)-edge factors uniquely as an \(f\)-edge followed by an \(e\)-edge. The present construction replaces that permutation by a general unitary matrix. As a result, the product \(L_{e_i}L_{f_j}\) need not correspond to a single reordered product, but may instead be a linear combination of such products.

A central structural question is when two such algebras are the same from the point of view of operator algebra theory. These algebras are classified up to isometric isomorphism in terms of the associated unitary matrix \(u\). In other words, the matrix \(u\) contains the essential information determining the algebra, subject to the natural equivalences arising from changes of basis in the two families of generators. Thus, understanding the unitary commutation matrix provides a complete invariant for the isometric isomorphism class of the algebra.
outputs.L4:
This text investigates a class of nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by two families of operators whose mixed products satisfy prescribed unitary commutation relations. These relations are encoded by an \(nm \times nm\) unitary matrix \(u\), which determines how generators from one family commute past generators from the other. In this way, the algebras generalize the analytic Toeplitz algebras associated with rank-2 single-vertex graphs, where the commutation rules are typically governed by a permutation matrix. Allowing an arbitrary unitary matrix produces a broader and more flexible framework while retaining the essential structure of higher-rank graph-type operator algebras.

The main focus is the classification of these algebras up to isometric isomorphism. The text shows that the defining unitary matrix \(u\) is the fundamental invariant: two such nonselfadjoint operator algebras are isometrically isomorphic precisely when their corresponding unitary commutation data agree in the appropriate sense. Thus, the algebraic and operator-space structure of the algebra completely remembers the unitary relation used to define it. This result identifies the matrix \(u\) not merely as a construction parameter, but as the decisive object controlling the isometric isomorphism class of the algebra.

Consequently, the study provides a unified perspective on analytic Toeplitz algebras arising from rank-2 single-vertex graphs and their unitary deformations. It demonstrates that the passage from permutation-based commutation relations to general unitary relations does not obscure classification; instead, the unitary matrix remains visible as the key invariant. The work therefore clarifies the role of unitary commutation relations in the structure theory of nonselfadjoint operator algebras and establishes a precise classification theorem for this family of examples.
outputs.L5:
These mathematical structures, known as **Toeplitz matrices**, play an important role in linear algebra, signal processing, statistics, and numerical analysis. A Toeplitz matrix is a matrix in which each descending diagonal from left to right has constant values. In other words, every element depends only on the difference between its row and column indices.

For example:

\[
\begin{bmatrix}
a & b & c \\
d & a & b \\
e & d & a
\end{bmatrix}
\]

is a Toeplitz matrix because each diagonal contains the same repeated element. These matrices are useful because their special structure allows many computations to be performed more efficiently than with general matrices. Toeplitz systems often appear when working with time series, convolution operations, and discretized differential equations.

These properties make Toeplitz matrices a valuable tool in both theoretical mathematics and practical applications.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main idea of a paper about nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by two families of isometries satisfying unitary commutation relations.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper studies nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by two “row” families of isometries that interact through prescribed unitary commutation relations. Concretely, one has isometries \(S_1,\dots,S_m\) and \(T_1,\dots,T_n\), and the way an \(S_i\) passes past a \(T_j\) is governed by a fixed unitary matrix. Thus the algebra is a two-variable analogue of the tensor algebra of a Cuntz-type system, but with a unitary “twist” coupling the two directions.

The main idea is to understand these algebras through their representations and dilations. The authors show that contractive or isometric representations satisfying the commutation rules can often be dilated to better-behaved representations, such as defect-free or unitary-type representations. This allows them to identify structural invariants of the algebra, analyze its universal operator algebra, and relate it to the associated \(C^*\)-algebra or \(C^*\)-envelope.

In broad terms, the paper connects three themes:

1. **Nonselfadjoint operator algebras** generated by isometries.
2. **Twisted commutation relations** encoded by a unitary matrix.
3. **Dilation and representation theory**, used to determine the algebra’s structure and its \(C^*\)-cover.

So the central contribution is a framework for treating two interacting isometric systems as a single operator-algebraic object, with the unitary commutation relations controlling both the algebraic structure and the representation theory.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract-style description of operator algebras with generators \(L_{e_i}\) and \(L_{f_j}\) subject to relations determined by an \(nm \times nm\) unitary matrix \(u\).
counterfactuals.output:
We study nonselfadjoint operator algebras generated by row contractions
\[
L_e=(L_{e_1},\dots,L_{e_n}),\qquad L_f=(L_{f_1},\dots,L_{f_m}),
\]
whose mixed commutation relations are encoded by a unitary matrix
\[
u\in M_{nm}(\mathbb C).
\]
Specifically, the generators satisfy relations of the form
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
=
\sum_{k=1}^n\sum_{\ell=1}^m
u_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\,L_{f_\ell}L_{e_k},
\]
while the \(e\)- and \(f\)-families are otherwise freely generated. These algebras may be viewed as unitary-twisted analogues of higher-rank graph or tensor algebras, interpolating between free semigroup algebras and product systems over \(\mathbb N^2\). The unitary \(u\) governs the interaction between the two sets of creation operators and determines the resulting representation theory, dilation theory, and isomorphism invariants. Such algebras provide a natural framework for studying noncommutative analytic functions, covariance relations, and C\(^*\)-envelopes associated with unitary commutation rules.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain in one paragraph how analytic Toeplitz algebras of rank-2 graphs with one vertex can be generalized using unitary commutation relations.
counterfactuals.output:
Analytic Toeplitz algebras of rank-2 graphs with one vertex can be generalized by replacing the graph’s combinatorial commutation rule between edges of the two colors with an arbitrary unitary commutation relation. In the rank-2 graph case, if the blue edges are \(e_1,\dots,e_m\) and the red edges are \(f_1,\dots,f_n\), the factorization rule is encoded by a permutation \(\theta\) such that \(e_i f_j = f_{j'} e_{i'}\). More generally, one takes finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces \(E\) and \(F\), representing the two edge types, and a unitary map \(U:E\otimes F\to F\otimes E\). This unitary specifies relations of the form  
\[
e_i f_j=\sum_{k,\ell} U_{(k,\ell),(i,j)}\, f_k e_\ell,
\]
rather than merely permuting basis elements. The associated analytic Toeplitz algebra is then generated by creation operators on the Fock space of the resulting product system over \(\mathbb N^2\), subject to these unitary commutation relations. When \(U\) is a permutation unitary, one recovers the usual rank-2 graph Toeplitz algebra; arbitrary unitaries therefore provide a natural “noncommutative” or “twisted” generalization.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Give a brief mathematical overview of algebras generated by \(L_{e_1},\ldots,L_{e_n}\) and \(L_{f_1},\ldots,L_{f_m}\) satisfying \(L_{e_i}L_{f_j}=\sum_{k,l}u_{i,j,k,l}L_{f_l}L_{e_k}\), including their classification.
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(u=(u_{i,j,k,l})\) be a unitary matrix on \(\mathbb C^n\otimes \mathbb C^m\), written with indices
\[
1\le i,k\le n,\qquad 1\le j,l\le m.
\]
One studies the nonselfadjoint operator algebra \(\mathcal A_u\) generated by symbols
\[
L_{e_1},\dots,L_{e_n},\qquad L_{f_1},\dots,L_{f_m}
\]
subject to the unitary commutation relations
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}
=
\sum_{k=1}^n\sum_{l=1}^m
u_{i,j,k,l}\,L_{f_l}L_{e_k}.
\]

## 1. Basic interpretation

The \(e_i\)’s and \(f_j\)’s may be viewed as two “colours” of generators. The relation says that every word with an \(e\)-letter followed by an \(f\)-letter can be uniquely rewritten as a linear combination of words with the \(f\)-letter first and the \(e\)-letter second. The unitarity of \(u\) guarantees that this rewriting rule is coherent and gives a product system over \(\mathbb N^2\).

Equivalently, \(\mathcal A_u\) is the tensor algebra of a product system \(X_u\) with fibres
\[
X_{(1,0)}\cong \mathbb C^n,\qquad X_{(0,1)}\cong \mathbb C^m,
\]
and multiplication determined by the unitary map
\[
u:\mathbb C^n\otimes \mathbb C^m\to \mathbb C^m\otimes \mathbb C^n.
\]

The canonical representation is the Fock representation, where \(L_{e_i}\) and \(L_{f_j}\) act as left creation operators. The norm-closed algebra they generate is often denoted \(\mathcal A_u\).

## 2. Special cases

### Commuting case

If \(n=m=1\) and \(u=(1)\), then the relation is simply
\[
L_eL_f=L_fL_e,
\]
so one obtains the bidisk-type algebra generated by two commuting shifts.

More generally, if \(u\) is the flip unitary
\[
e_i\otimes f_j\mapsto f_j\otimes e_i,
\]
then
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}=L_{f_j}L_{e_i},
\]
so the two families commute.

### Permutation case

If \(u\) is a permutation matrix, then for each pair \((i,j)\) there is a unique pair \((k,l)\) such that
\[
L_{e_i}L_{f_j}=L_{f_l}L_{e_k}.
\]
This gives the semigroup algebra of a single-vertex \(2\)-graph, or rank-two graph, with \(n\) blue edges and \(m\) red edges.

### General unitary case

For a general unitary \(u\), the relation is not deterministic; moving an \(e\)-letter past an \(f\)-letter produces a linear combination of words. These are “unitary commutation relations” and give noncommutative analogues of higher-rank graph algebras.

## 3. Universal property

The algebra \(\mathcal A_u\) is universal for row contractions
\[
E=(E_1,\dots,E_n),\qquad F=(F_1,\dots,F_m)
\]
satisfying
\[
E_iF_j=\sum_{k,l}u_{i,j,k,l}F_lE_k.
\]
In the isometric version, the rows \(E\) and \(F\) are row isometries.

Thus \(\mathcal A_u\) is the universal norm-closed operator algebra generated by two rows obeying the prescribed unitary commutation rule.

## 4. Gauge action and grading

There is a natural gauge action of \(\mathbb T^2\) given by
\[
\gamma_{z,w}(L_{e_i})=zL_{e_i},\qquad 
\gamma_{z,w}(L_{f_j})=wL_{f_j}.
\]
This gives \(\mathcal A_u\) a natural \(\mathbb N^2\)-grading. The homogeneous component of degree \((p,q)\) is spanned by words containing \(p\) \(e\)-letters and \(q\) \(f\)-letters.

## 5. Classification

The main classification is by the unitary \(u\), modulo changes of basis in the \(e\)-space and the \(f\)-space.

Let \(u\) act as
\[
u:\mathbb C^n\otimes\mathbb C^m\to \mathbb C^m\otimes\mathbb C^n.
\]
Two algebras \(\mathcal A_u\) and \(\mathcal A_v\) are graded completely isometrically isomorphic precisely when the corresponding unitaries are product-unitarily equivalent: there exist unitaries
\[
A\in U(n),\qquad B\in U(m)
\]
such that
\[
v=(B\otimes A)\,u\,(A\otimes B)^*.
\]
In coordinates, this corresponds to changing generators by
\[
L_{e_i}\mapsto \sum_{p}A_{p i}L_{e_p},
\qquad
L_{f_j}\mapsto \sum_{q}B_{q j}L_{f_q}.
\]

For ungraded isomorphisms one also allows the possible interchange of the two colours. Thus, up to swapping the \(e\)- and \(f\)-families, the invariant is the product-unitary equivalence class of \(u\).

If \(n\neq m\), the two colours cannot generally be interchanged because their multiplicities differ. If \(n=m\), one may also compare \(u\) with the flipped inverse unitary obtained by solving the relation for \(L_{f_j}L_{e_i}\) and then relabelling the \(f\)’s as \(e\)’s and the \(e\)’s as \(f\)’s.

In short:

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal A_u\cong \mathcal A_v
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
u\text{ and }v\text{ are product-unitarily equivalent, up to colour exchange.}
}
\]

## 6. Summary

These algebras are tensor algebras of \(\mathbb N^2\)-product systems determined by a unitary commutation matrix \(u\). They generalize both commuting multivariable shift algebras and rank-two graph algebras. Their structure is governed by the way the \(e\)-generators and \(f\)-generators braid past one another, and their classification is essentially the classification of the unitary \(u\) up to independent unitary changes of basis in the two generating spaces, with a possible swap of the two colours.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a short research-style summary of the classification of nonselfadjoint operator algebras associated to a unitary matrix \(u\) via commutation relations between \(e\)- and \(f\)-generators.
counterfactuals.output:
A standard construction associates to a unitary matrix  
\[
u\in M_{mn}(\mathbb C)\simeq B(\mathbb C^m\otimes \mathbb C^n)
\]
a nonselfadjoint operator algebra generated by two families
\[
e_1,\dots,e_m,\qquad f_1,\dots,f_n
\]
subject to row-contraction/isometric relations and the unitary commutation rule
\[
e_i f_j=\sum_{k=1}^m\sum_{\ell=1}^n u_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\, f_\ell e_k .
\]
Equivalently, \(u\) is the structure map of a product system over \(\mathbb N^2\), and the resulting tensor algebra is often denoted \(\mathcal A_u\) or \(\mathcal T_+(X_u)\). Its C\(^*\)-envelope is the corresponding Cuntz–Pimsner algebra.

The classification problem asks when two such algebras \(\mathcal A_u\) and \(\mathcal A_v\) are isomorphic, completely isometrically isomorphic, or isomorphic in a graded/gauge-preserving sense. The basic invariant is the unitary commutation tensor \(u\), but only up to natural changes of bases in the \(e\)- and \(f\)-coordinates. If \(A\in U(m)\) and \(B\in U(n)\), then replacing
\[
e_i\mapsto \sum_p A_{pi}e_p,\qquad f_j\mapsto \sum_q B_{qj}f_q
\]
transforms \(u\) by product-unitary equivalence. In tensor notation this has the form
\[
v=(B\otimes A)\,u\,(A\otimes B)^*,
\]
up to the convention used for ordering the tensor factors. Thus product-unitary equivalence of \(u\) and \(v\) yields a completely isometric isomorphism \(\mathcal A_u\simeq \mathcal A_v\). If \(m=n\), one also has a possible color-exchange symmetry interchanging the \(e\)- and \(f\)-generators, corresponding to replacing \(u\) by the flipped inverse/adjoint commutation matrix.

A useful analytic invariant is the character space. Characters are determined by scalars \(z=(z_i)\in\overline{\mathbb B}_m\) and \(w=(w_j)\in\overline{\mathbb B}_n\) satisfying the scalar version of the commutation relations:
\[
z_i w_j=\sum_{k,\ell}u_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}\,w_\ell z_k .
\]
The corresponding affine variety
\[
\Omega_u=\{(z,w): z_iw_j=\sum_{k,\ell}u_{(i,j),(k,\ell)}w_\ell z_k\}
\]
is invariant under algebra isomorphism. In many nondegenerate cases, biholomorphic equivalence of these varieties, together with the row-ball structure, forces precisely the product-unitary equivalence described above.

For permutation unitaries \(u\), the relations reduce to
\[
e_i f_j=f_{\ell}e_k
\]
for a permutation \(\theta(i,j)=(k,\ell)\) of \(\{1,\dots,m\}\times\{1,\dots,n\}\). These are the single-vertex rank-two graph or \(2\)-graph algebras. Their classification becomes combinatorial: two such algebras are equivalent when the underlying permutations are conjugate by relabelings of the \(e\)- and \(f\)-edges, i.e. by the natural action of \(S_m\times S_n\), again with a possible color flip when \(m=n\).

In summary, the classification of the nonselfadjoint algebras associated to a unitary commutation matrix \(u\) is governed by the unitary tensor \(u\) modulo the natural symmetries coming from independent unitary changes of basis in the \(e\)- and \(f\)-generators, and, in square cases, interchange of the two colors. Analytic invariants such as the character variety \(\Omega_u\), gauge actions, and the C\(^*\)-envelope provide complementary formulations of the same classification principle.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
